chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from 'Umar ibn Yazid, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever prays Friday prayer with the non-Friday prayer and the hypocrites, he must repeat the prayer whether in travel or in residence.'

Thus, the meaning of this report is to encourage the one who prayed with the non-Friday prayer and the hypocrites to consider what he prayed as part of the voluntary prayers (nafl) and to restart the prayer to attain the merit of these two surahs (prayers), and that which clarifies what we mentioned.

key_terms.بِغَيْرِ الْجُمُعَةِ: With the non-Friday prayer (or prayer of the hypocrites)
key_terms.فَضْلَ هَاتَيْنِ السُّورَتَيْنِ: The merit of these two surahs (prayers)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on repeating Friday prayer if performed with the hypocrites?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies that the instruction to 'repeat' the prayer does not necessarily mean invalidity, but rather a recommendation to re-perform it as Fard to secure the specific spiritual merit of Friday, distinguishing it from the status of Nafl (voluntary) prayer. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the distinct ontological value of Salat al-Jumu'ah, where performing it alongside the hypocrites or as a general prayer may suffice for obligation but lacks the full reward unless performed with the specific intention and context of Friday. The hadith thus serves as a practical guide for believers to maximize their spiritual gain by ensuring their Friday prayer is not merely a mechanical fulfillment of duty but a distinct act of worship aligned with the day's sanctity.
